summary: Reserved pool p99 latency spike after sidecar logging burst caused socket policing & autoscaler stall
description:
Issue Summary:
Customer (Nimbus Analytics) reported a sudden p99 latency spike (6–8x baseline) across several reserved-pool routes at ~13:05 UTC. Spike correlated with sustained high socket write queue lengths on sidecar processes attached to the reserved GPU pool. Autoscaler did not provision additional slots during the window, causing queueing to amplify for ~22 minutes before a partial self-recovery.

Impact:
- Affected 3 critical routes used by Nimbus: /v1/generate-chat, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank.
- Observed p99 generation latency from 220ms -> 1.7s. Client-reported timeouts at 30s (few).
- Customer on Dedicated (reserved capacity) — visible throughput loss and higher unit latency charges during incident window.

Timeline (UTC):
- 13:03: first small log flood from a tenant-side batch job (customer-side) observed in sidecar logs.
- 13:05: p50/p95 stable, p99 begins climbing; socket write queues in sidecars grow (metric socket_queue_depth > 5000).
- 13:07: autoscaler sampling window sees increased latency but not sustained CPU/GPU usage; scaling decision deferred.
- 13:18: sidecar log subsystem enters backpressure mode and kernel-level socket policing (skbuff drops) observed on nodes.
- 13:27: transient recovery as customer's batch completes; services return to baseline by ~13:30.

Steps to reproduce (observed when customer replayed a local load test):
1) Start many small short-lived streams with aggressive logging enabled on client side (debug mode).
2) Streams open persistent connections to reserved pool endpoints and emit frequent structured logs.
3) Sidecar process write buffers accumulate and kernel-level socket queuing spikes; if concurrent tenant load > baseline, p99 increases.

Observed metrics & logs (snips):
- sidecar.socket_queue_depth{pool=reserv-07} = 5.2k @ 13:10 UTC
- serving_runtime.request_latency.p99{route=/v1/generate-chat} = 1.7s @ 13:12 UTC
- Node syslog: "NET_TX_DROP: socket_policing: drop on dev eth0 due to skb_overflow"
- journald (sidecar): repeated "backpressure: write buffer full, throttling"
- autoscaler.log: "sampling window: insufficient stable CPU/GPU increase, no scale event"

Immediate mitigation applied by SRE:
- 13:22 UTC: reduced sidecar log level for affected tenant via per-tenant config -> queue depth began to decline.
- 13:24 UTC: enabled temporary per-sidecar socket write queue caps and increased autoscaler sensitivity (reduced min observation window from 120s to 45s) for the reserved pool.
- 13:31 UTC: queue depths returned to baseline and p99 dropped to normal.

Notes:
- Customer confirmed they had an internal scheduled batch in debug logging mode that correlates with the start of the spike.
- Autoscaler misread: it relies primarily on GPU utilization and average latency signals; short-duration socket queue amplification can elevate p99 without significantly changing GPU utilization, causing no scale decision.

investigation_notes:
Findings so far:
- Root chain: customer-side batch + debug logging -> sidecar write buffers saturated -> kernel socket policing/drops -> elevated p99 due to request write stalls.
- Autoscaler gap: scaling logic uses GPU busy and stable latency averages; it did not interpret transient socket queuing as a sustained capacity shortage.
- Sidecar behavior: when facing sustained write buffer pressure the sidecar falls back to in-process buffering with limited backpressure signals upstream; this allows requests to queue locally without a clear upstream signal that autoscaler observes.
Evidence & dashboards:
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/POOL/reserved-07-telemetry?from=2026-03-13T13:00:00Z&to=2026-03-13T14:00:00Z
- Kernel logs: /var/log/journal/node-07/syslog (attached snippet in ticket).
- Customer trace: Nimbus provided session replay ids: nimbus-replay-20260313-1.
Hypotheses to validate:
1) Modify autoscaler to consider socket_queue_depth and sidecar backpressure metrics as auxiliary signals for short-window scale-ups.
2) Patch sidecar to emit explicit backpressure metrics and expose per-tenant socket queue sizes to control-plane telemetry.
3) Add defensive per-tenant logging-rate limits at the gateway to prevent tenant-induced log floods from impacting node-level buffers.
Next investigative steps:
- Run controlled replay against a staging reserved pool to reproduce queue growth and test autoscaler sensitivity adjustments.
- Instrument sidecar to emit backpressure event metrics (PR linked below).
resolution:
Mitigation in place (temporary): lowered tenant log level, applied qdisc caps on nodes, adjusted autoscaler sampling to be more sensitive for this pool.
Permanent work items (assigned):
- Sidecar code change to emit backpressure metrics and per-tenant socket queue sizes (PR #4521) -> target patch 2026-03-20.
- Autoscaler enhancement to include sidecar backpressure as a fast-path signal for reserved pools -> design doc in Confluence.
- Add gateway-level per-tenant logging rate-limiter to prevent similar log floods.
Follow-up assigned to Infra team (Marcus Nguyen) and Product for autoscaler changes. Expected customer follow-up call scheduled 2026-03-15.
public_notes: Customer-facing summary prepared: transient p99 spike caused by customer debug log flood that saturated sidecar write buffers. Temporary mitigations applied; long-term fixes planned. Customer notified and scheduled follow-up.
